Name: Avoid checkpanic
Short Description: Using `checkpanic` lets an unhandled error panic and crash the program instead of being handled.
Long Description: The `checkpanic` expression causes the program to panic and terminate abruptly when the checked expression evaluates to an error, instead of allowing the error to be handled. Prefer `check` with explicit error handling so callers can recover instead of crashing.

Name: Unused function parameter
Short Description: A function parameter is declared but never used within the function body.
Long Description: A function parameter that is declared but never referenced in the function body adds noise, misleads readers about the function's behavior, and may indicate incomplete implementation or a leftover from refactoring.

Name: Non isolated public function
Short Description: A public function is not marked `isolated`, so it cannot be safely called from concurrently executing isolated code.
Long Description: A public function that is not marked `isolated` cannot be safely invoked from concurrently executing isolated code or workers without the compiler being able to prove the absence of data races, limiting how the function can be reused in concurrent contexts.

Name: Non isolated public method
Short Description: A public method is not marked `isolated`, so it cannot be safely called from concurrently executing isolated code.
Long Description: A public object method that is not marked `isolated` cannot be safely invoked from concurrently executing isolated code or workers without the compiler being able to prove the absence of data races, limiting how the method can be reused in concurrent contexts.

Name: Non isolated public class
Short Description: A public class is not marked `isolated`, limiting how safely its instances can be shared across concurrent code.
Long Description: A public class that is not marked `isolated` limits how safely its instances can be shared and accessed across concurrently executing isolated code or workers.

Name: Non isolated public object
Short Description: A public object type is not marked `isolated`, limiting how safely its instances can be shared across concurrent code.
Long Description: A public object constructor/type that is not marked `isolated` limits how safely its instances can be shared and accessed across concurrently executing isolated code or workers.

Name: This operation always evaluates to true
Short Description: A binary operation always evaluates to `true` regardless of its operands' runtime values.
Long Description: This binary operation always evaluates to `true` regardless of the runtime value of its operands, based on the semantics of the operator and a constant operand (e.g. comparisons against `int:MAX_VALUE`/`float:Infinity`, or short-circuiting with a literal `true`/`false`). This is usually unintended and indicates dead logic or a mistake in the condition.

Name: This operation always evaluates to false
Short Description: A binary operation always evaluates to `false` regardless of its operands' runtime values.
Long Description: This binary operation always evaluates to `false` regardless of the runtime value of its operands, based on the semantics of the operator and a constant operand (e.g. comparisons against `int:MAX_VALUE`/`int:MIN_VALUE`/`float:Infinity`). This is usually unintended and indicates dead logic or a mistake in the condition.

Name: This operation always evaluates to the same value
Short Description: A binary operation always reduces to one of its own operands, making the operation itself redundant.
Long Description: This binary operation always reduces to the value of one of its own operands regardless of the other (e.g. `a || false`, `a && true`), making the operation itself redundant and the code harder to read.

Name: This variable is assigned to itself
Short Description: A variable is assigned to itself, which has no effect and usually signals a mistake.
Long Description: Assigning a variable to itself has no effect and is usually a mistake, such as a typo where a different variable or field was intended on one side of the assignment.

Name: Unused class private fields
Short Description: A private class field is declared but never read or written outside its own declaration.
Long Description: A private class field that is never read or written outside of its own declaration serves no purpose and should be removed, as it adds maintenance overhead without contributing to the class's behavior.

Name: Invalid range expression
Short Description: A range expression's bounds never produce any elements, making it dead code.
Long Description: A range expression whose lower bound is greater than (or, for the inclusive `...` operator, greater than or equal to) its upper bound never produces any elements, so any loop or operation over it is dead code.

Name: Hard-coded secrets are security-sensitive
Short Description: A secret such as a password, API key, or token is embedded as a literal value in source code.
Long Description: Embedding secrets such as passwords, API keys, or tokens directly as literal values in source code exposes them to anyone with access to the codebase or its version history, and makes rotating a compromised secret require a code change and redeploy.

Name: Non configurable secrets are security-sensitive
Short Description: A secret is assigned a fixed value instead of being exposed as a configurable one.
Long Description: A secret that is assigned a fixed value rather than being exposed as a configurable value forces the same secret to be reused across environments and prevents it from being rotated or overridden without modifying and redeploying the code.
